1410988692253118476.a: If you have only used Windows PCs you might have no idea what a UNIX system is... Well, generally, most things not-Microsoft at this point. UNIX itself is dead but most devices (non-PC) run UNIX-like systems based on either Linux or macOS. How about a little historical review:

1410988694006386688.a:
In 1988 Steve Jobs and company at NeXT built NeXTSTEP which evolved directly into macOS and iOS of today. This was based on MIT Mach Kernel and Berkeley BSD UNIX user space with a revolutionary object oriented desktop UI.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NeXTSTEP

1410988695793119236.a:
macOS started out in 1984 as a scratch built not-at-all-UNIX system with bare minimum features. Pretty quick people wanted UNIX on this hardware. So Apple developed Apple A/UX based on AT&T UNIX. It ran UNIX and Mac apps natively. Neither well.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A/UX

1410988697445675009.a:
About that time an effort to recreate UNIX without using AT&T copyright or trademark materials was nearing completion as The GNU System. It had no kernel and often used the SUNOS kernel on SUN computers.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU

1410988699135926277.a:
NeXT computers were expensive and they needed money so they ported the UI and Objective-C to Windows and other UNIX systems. Microsoft promoted OPENSTEP as the next desktop for WIndows NT. Many fell for it. NT4 included Explorer; a Norton Commander clone.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenStep#…

1410988700822032387.a:
GNU needed a desktop (and still had no kernel) so they jumped on the OPENSTEP bandwagon and built an impressive implementation. That looked like a Soviet apartment block. No one used it except to port individual apps to UNIX+X11.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenStep#…

1410988702466183169.a:
Linus Torvalds decided to build a kernel for 386 PCs. This ended up directly competing with Microsoft Windows after a few years. GNU users pretty instantly yoinked the Linux kernel in place of their SUNOS kernel. Useful SUNOS features were cloned by Linux.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux

1410988704039116805.a:
Apple was dying from having a pretty useless operating system on fairly impressive hardware. Ultimately they uncled and bought NeXT and Steve Jobs as a last hope. NeXTSTEP was renamed MacOS X. Today this is macOS.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS

1410988705733545985.a:
Steve Jobs finally was able to realize his vision of a pocket sized music store and quickly that became his ultimate dream of a pocket sized computer called iPhone. This used a version of macOS called iOS. You probably have heard of it.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS

1410988707394600962.a:
Basically everyone started trying to replicate iPhone but their operating systems were often outdated garbage duct taped to work at all. A few folks built Android and most handheld devices use that today. Android is a non-GNU user space for Linux.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(…)

1410988709160308738.a:
Today Microsoft is in the embarrassing position of having to build Windows 11 so it natively runs Linux and Android software to hedge its bets. This is a trap of course but given their history I expect it to go nowhere like everything they do.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_11
